description: The exporter configuration. See docs/CONFIGURATION.md. Collectors are defined under collectors, in the files collector_files lists, or both.

^x-.+.description: The file's own, ignored by the exporter: a place for YAML anchors (&name) the rest of the file reuses with aliases (*name) and merge keys (<<: *name).

collector_files.description: Further files of collectors, as paths or glob patterns such as collectors.d/*.yaml, relative to this file. A collector file holds a collectors list and nothing else. See docs/CONFIGURATION.md#collector-files.

collectors.description: The collectors. A probe names one with its collector parameter. A name must be unique across this list and every collector file.

items.description: How to reach a kind of target and turn its response into metrics.

cache.description: The collector's response cache. See docs/CONFIGURATION.md#response-caching.

stale_if_error.description: After ttl, keep a result this much longer to answer a probe whose trip to the target fails, marked by http_exporter_result_stale 1. Omit or 0s to answer the failure.

ttl.description: Answer a repeat of the same probe from memory for this long. Omit or 0s to always go to the target.

coalesce.description: Share one request to the target among identical probes that arrive while it is in flight. Defaults to true.

type.description: How to decode the response. Defaults to auto, which the transform or the Content-Type decides.

on_decode_error.description: fail stops the probe, log carries on and logs why, ignore carries on quietly. Defaults to fail.

on_fetch_error.description: fail stops the probe, log carries on and logs why, ignore carries on quietly. Defaults to fail.

on_transform_error.description: fail stops the probe, log carries on and logs why, ignore carries on quietly. Defaults to fail.

max_output_bytes.description: The most bytes one answer of the collector's Python worker may be, a script's metrics or a pre-script's data. A size: a whole number of bytes, or a number with a unit such as 512KiB, 10MB or 1.5GiB, under 2^63 bytes. At least 38 bytes, the answer of a script that emits no metric; 0, like the key left out, is the default, 1MiB. The range, and the least of a size written as text, in quotes or with a unit, are checked by the exporter when the configuration loads.

max_response_bytes.description: The most bytes of an answer the collector reads, decompressed, whatever its request.max_response_bytes; the smaller of the two wins. A size: a whole number of bytes, or a number with a unit such as 512KiB, 10MB or 1.5GiB, under 2^63 bytes. At least 1KiB, since a limit under it is one whose unit was left out; 0, like the key left out, is the default. The range, and the least of a size written as text, in quotes or with a unit, are checked by the exporter when the configuration loads.

max_script_memory.description: The most memory, as address space, each of the collector's Python workers may use, the interpreter and its libraries included, such as 256MiB. A script that needs more fails with a MemoryError. At least 32MiB; 0, the default, leaves it unbounded. Enforced on Linux.

script_timeout.description: How long a Python script may run. Starting the interpreter is not counted. At least 1ms, which the exporter checks when the configuration loads; defaults to 100ms.

max_concurrent_probes.description: How many trips to its targets the collector makes at once; a probe over the limit is answered 503 at once, a static target waits. Omit or 0 for the default, 32.

metrics.description: The metric rules. No two of them may be the same rule, alike in name, expression, items, labels, value_map and time_format: each would make every series the other makes, and every scrape would fail on a duplicate series. Nor, under a prometheus transform, may the expression of one rule match the name another rule passes on the metric of, where the two give its series one name and the same labels: each would make every series of that metric. A rule with an expression whose type is histogram or summary and whose error_mode is not fail is about the metrics of that type alone, and may match such a name unless the rule of the name sets that type too. The exporter checks both when the configuration loads. A python collector's rules make no series and are not held to it.

error_mode.description: What happens when this metric cannot be extracted. Defaults to log. Not for the python transform, whose script fails the scrape itself, with fail(...).

expression.description: Where the value comes from, in the transform's language: jq, a regex, a CSS selector, an XPath expression, a CSV column or a source metric pattern.

items.description: jq, yq and css only: selects the things the metric is about, such as table rows. The expression and labels are then evaluated once per item: for jq and yq with the item as . and the whole document as $root, for css as selectors within the item.
Set value for a static label, or expression to read it from the response.

expression.description: Reads the label from the response, in the transform's language, like the metric's expression. Not blanks alone: a constant is a value.

name.description: The label's name: letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit. Under the collector's name_escaping underscores or values it may be any name, such as service.name, and is exported escaped. A name transform.rename_labels renames or transform.remove_labels removes is not exported, and may be any name. Text: a name YAML reads as a number or a boolean is written in quotes.

required.description: expression labels only: a series the expression gives no value, or an empty one, fails the metric under its error_mode instead of being exported without the label. Defaults to false.

truncate.description: Cut a value longer than limits.max_label_value_length to fit, ending in …, instead of failing the scrape.

value.description: A static label value, exported as written. May contain {{param_name}} placeholders, filled from the probe's parameters; see docs/REQUESTS.md#in-label-values.

value_map.description: Turns the value the label's expression gives into another, such as {"1": running}; "*" maps any value it does not list, and a value mapped to "" leaves the label off. Without a match and without "*", the value is kept.

name.description: The metric name, before metrics_prefix: letters, digits, _ and :, not starting with a digit. Under the collector's name_escaping underscores or values it may be any name, such as http.server.duration, and is exported escaped. Text: a name YAML reads as a number or a boolean, such as 404 or true, is written in quotes.

required.description: When false, a missing value is skipped without an error. Defaults to true. Not for the python transform, whose rules read no value.

scale.description: Multiplies the value, mapped or read as a number, such as 0.001 for milliseconds to seconds. Finite and not 0. Not for the python transform; for prometheus, plain samples only.

time_format.description: Reads the text the expression gives as a time; the value is that time in Unix seconds. rfc3339, rfc1123, or a layout: the reference time Mon Jan 2 15:04:05 MST 2006 written as the text writes its times, such as "2006-01-02 15:04:05", with a year, a month and a day. scale applies after. Not with value_map, and not for the prometheus and python transforms.

time_zone.description: With time_format: the zone a text that names none of its own is read in, as an IANA name such as Europe/Sofia. Defaults to UTC.

value_map.description: Turns the text the expression gives into the value, such as {up: 1, down: 0}; "*" maps any value it does not list, numbers included. Without a match and without "*", the value is read as a number. Not for the prometheus and python transforms.

metrics_prefix.description: Joined with _ to the front of every metric the collector exports, such as grafana for grafana_statuspage_status. Letters and digits, in parts joined by single underscores.

name.description: Unique name, used as the collector parameter of /probe.

name_escaping.description: What to do with a metric or label name that is not a classic Prometheus name, such as http.server.duration: fail the scrape (the default), replace what a classic name may not have with underscores, or use Prometheus's reversible values encoding (U__…). A name the collector writes itself, a rule's or a label's, is held to the same when the configuration loads: refused under fail, exported escaped under the other two. See docs/CONFIGURATION.md#utf-8-names.

request.description: How the collector reaches its data. See docs/REQUESTS.md, docs/LOCALFILE.md for localfile, docs/GRAPHITE.md for graphite, docs/GRPC.md for grpc, docs/SSHFILE.md for sshfile, docs/SQL.md for sql, docs/DNS.md for dns, docs/TLSCERT.md for tlscert, docs/S3FILE.md for s3file and docs/KUBERNETES.md for kubernetes.

accept_codes.description: grpc: the gRPC status codes other than OK whose calls are answers rather than failures, by name, such as [NOT_FOUND]. Such a call is not retried; its rules see an empty object, the code as $status and the status message as $headers["grpc-message"].

accept_status.description: The HTTP statuses whose answers are decoded, such as [200, 503] or ["2xx", 503]; every 2xx when left out. Any other status fails the scrape in the http_status stage. An accepted status is not retried. http and graphite.

access_key_id_file.description: s3file, with secret_access_key_file: the file of a static access key's ID, read at every request. Without the two the AWS SDK's default chain finds the credentials: the environment, a web identity token (IRSA), the shared files, the container's or the instance's role. See docs/S3FILE.md#credentials.

all_namespaces.description: kubernetes: list the resource across the cluster, every namespace's objects, or a cluster-scoped resource's, such as nodes. Not with namespaces. Defaults to false.

allowed_targets.description: Hosts, globs such as *.example.com, IP addresses and CIDR networks the collector's requests may reach: a target is allowed when its host matches by name, or every address it resolves to is in an allowed network. Checked before the request, on every redirect and on every connection. Written in ASCII, as a target's host is: an internationalised name is listed, and requested, in its xn-- form. http, graphite, grpc, sshfile, sql and tlscert; dns matches its names by name alone, and a PTR target by address; for s3file, whose target is a bucket, the buckets it may read, by name or glob, and no address.

api_server.description: kubernetes: the URL of an API server other than the one of the cluster the exporter runs in, https, with a path when it is behind one; reached with tls.ca_file and bearer_token_file, or tls.cert_file and tls.key_file, each read at every scrape. Left out, the exporter's own cluster's, with its pod's service account. See docs/KUBERNETES.md#outside-the-cluster.

args.description: sql: the values of the statement's placeholders, in order, as text; sent as values, never as SQL (bound, or written in quoted as literals by the clickhouse driver). May contain {{param_name}} placeholders.

username.description: http, graphite and grpc: the username sent in the Basic credential. Not with a colon, which ends the username in the credential (RFC 7617).

body.description: http: the request body. May contain {{param_name}} placeholders, written as |json, |number, |form, |xml or |raw: {{param_service|json}}. See docs/REQUESTS.md#in-the-body-headers-and-query.

connections.description: sql: how the collector keeps connections to a target, a server or Snowflake account, in a pool for each of its databases and accounts, the limits counting across them. A static target may set each key but max_targets for itself. See docs/SQL.md#connections.

idle_timeout.description: How long an idle connection is kept. Defaults to 5m; 0 keeps it as long as the collector is configured.

keepalive.description: How a kept connection is found broken.

check.description: tcp, the default: TCP keepalives on every connection. ping: every idle connection is pinged every interval.

interval.description: How often: the TCP keepalive interval, or how often the idle connections are pinged. At least 1s, which the exporter checks when the configuration loads; defaults to 30s; 0 checks none.

max_idle_per_target.description: How many connections to a target are kept idle between scrapes, across its databases and accounts. Defaults to 1; 0 keeps none.

max_lifetime.description: How long a connection is used before it is closed and made again. Defaults to 1h; 0 uses it as long as it works.

max_per_target.description: The most connections open to one target at once, across its databases and accounts, keepalive pings counted; a scrape beyond waits within its deadline for one. It bounds the target's pools, one for each database and account, too. Defaults to 2; 0 sets no limit to the connections and keeps at most 64 pools.

max_targets.description: The most targets, servers or Snowflake accounts, the collector keeps connections to, whatever databases and accounts it reaches there; at the limit the pools of the target used longest ago are closed. Defaults to 50; 0 sets no limit.

database.description: sql: the database the statement runs on; the account's default when left out. Not for oracle, which names it by service_name. May contain {{param_name}} placeholders, filled with letters, digits and _ - . $ only.

denied_targets.description: Hosts, globs, IP addresses and CIDR networks the collector's requests may not reach: a target matching by name, or resolving to any address in a denied network, is refused with 403. Wins over allowed_targets. Written in ASCII, as allowed_targets is.

descriptors.description: grpc, required but for grpc.health.v1.Health: where the message types come from. reflection asks the server's reflection service; protoset reads protoset_file; proto compiles proto_files.

driver.description: sql, required: the database's driver, in any case and with blanks around it or not, as the exporter matches it. mysql, postgres and sqlserver are built in; oracle, clickhouse, snowflake and vertica only in a build with SQL_DRIVERS naming them. See docs/SQL.md.

endpoint.description: s3file: the scheme, host and port of a store that speaks the S3 API, such as https://minio.example.com:9000, in place of AWS's. See docs/S3FILE.md#other-stores.

field_selector.description: kubernetes: the field selector sent with the listing, such as status.phase=Running, of the fields the resource can be selected by; every object when left out.

files.description: localfile, sshfile and s3file: read every file of the directory whose name matches one of these patterns (path.Match syntax, no /), each checked on its own and labelled file. Not with request.path. See docs/LOCALFILE.md#reading-a-directory.

follow_redirects.description: http and graphite: follow redirect statuses instead of answering with the redirect itself. A redirect that leaves the origin the request was made to — its scheme, host and port — is sent only Accept, Accept-Language and User-Agent, with the values the first request had, so a token must never be put in those three, and never the request body, and is refused over https when the collector has a tls.cert_file, unless its host is in redirect_trusted_hosts. Defaults to false. See docs/REQUESTS.md#what-a-followed-redirect-carries.

forward_headers.description: http, graphite and grpc: the headers a probe forwards to the target, from its header_<name> parameters. Not Authorization, which forward_authorization forwards, Accept-Encoding, which the exporter sets itself, or Host, Connection, Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, Trailer, TE, Upgrade and any Proxy- header, which describe the connection to the exporter; each would never be forwarded.

from.description: graphite: the start of the render window, as Graphite writes a time: -15min, the default, -1h, or Unix seconds. The from probe parameter overrides it.

group.description: kubernetes: the resource's API group, such as apps or cert-manager.io; left out for the core group, of pods, services and nodes, which has no name.

headers.description: http and graphite: headers sent to the target. A name is an HTTP token, letters, digits and !#$%&'*+-.^_`|~, set once whatever its case, and not Accept-Encoding, which the exporter sets itself. Values may contain {{param_name}} placeholders.

idle_timeout.description: sshfile: how long a connection nothing uses is kept. Defaults to 5m; 0 keeps it as long as the collector is configured.

keepalive_count_max.description: sshfile: how many keepalives in a row may go unanswered before the connection is closed and the next scrape makes a new one. At least 1; defaults to 3.

keepalive_interval.description: sshfile: how often a keepalive is sent on the connection kept to a host, and how long each is given to be answered. At least 1s, which the exporter checks when the configuration loads; defaults to 30s; 0 sends none.

known_hosts_file.description: sshfile, required: the known_hosts file the host's key is verified against, as ssh-keyscan writes its lines; hashed lines and [host]:port are read. The key is always verified. See docs/SSHFILE.md#host-keys.

label_selector.description: kubernetes: the label selector sent with the listing, such as app.kubernetes.io/part-of=shop,tier!=cache; every object when left out.

login.description: http and graphite: log in before the request and send the token the login gives, in Authorization as a bearer token unless header says otherwise. type json posts a JSON object of fields and field_files to url and reads the token from the answer; type oauth2 asks the token endpoint url with the OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant. No probe parameter sets or changes it. See docs/AUTHENTICATION.md#logging-in-to-a-target.

auth_style.description: oauth2: how the client's id and secret are sent: header, as a Basic credential, the default, or params, as parameters of the form.

client_id.description: oauth2: the client's id. Exactly one of client_id and client_id_file.

client_id_file.description: oauth2: the file holding the client's id, read at every login.

client_secret_file.description: oauth2: required. The file holding the client's secret, read at every login.

endpoint_params.description: oauth2: further parameters of the token request, such as audience or resource. Not grant_type, scope, client_id or client_secret, which the grant sets.

expires_in.description: json: the jq expression of the token's lifetime in seconds in the answer's body, such as .expires_in; null when the answer does not say. Left out, or null, ttl applies.

field_files.description: json: members of the JSON object posted, each read from its file at every login, such as {username: /var/run/secrets/login/username, password: /var/run/secrets/login/password}. Required: at least one. A field is in fields or here, not both.

fields.description: json: members of the JSON object posted, as written: for what is no secret, such as a tenant.

header.description: The header the token is sent in, Authorization when left out. Its name reads as a credential's — it has auth, token, key, session or the like in it — so that what shows a request's headers withholds it. Not with token_cookie, whose cookie is sent in Cookie.

prefix.description: What the token is sent after: "Bearer " in Authorization and nothing in another header when left out; "" sends the token alone. Not with token_cookie.

scopes.description: oauth2: the scopes asked for, sent as the scope parameter.

tls.description: The login's own tls settings, for a login server whose certificate the collector's request.tls does not verify; left out, request.tls. Never what a probe or a static target changes of request.tls.

token.description: json: the jq expression of the token in the answer's JSON body, such as .access_token, with $status and $headers as in a rule. Exactly one of token, token_header and token_cookie.

token_cookie.description: json: the cookie the answer sets that is the session, such as JSESSIONID; it is sent back in the Cookie header, and its Max-Age or Expires is its lifetime.

token_header.description: json: the header of the answer that holds the token, such as X-Subject-Token.

ttl.description: How long a token is used when the answer does not say: no expires_in, an oauth2 answer without expires_in, a cookie without Max-Age or Expires, a token_header. Left out, such a token is used until the target answers 401.

type.description: Required. json: post a JSON object of fields and field_files to url and read the token from the answer. oauth2: ask the token endpoint url for a token with the client credentials grant (RFC 6749 section 4.4).

url.description: Required. Where the login is sent: an absolute http or https URL, the same for every target, or a path from the root such as /api/login, resolved against the target's scheme, host and port alone, so each target is logged in to; a path relative to the target's is refused. Of a scheme allowed_schemes allows, held to allowed_targets and denied_targets; without credentials, a fragment or placeholders. A login follows no redirect.

max_age.description: localfile, sshfile and s3file: refuse a file last modified longer ago than this, so a writer that has stopped fails the scrape instead of exporting its last values forever.

max_files.description: localfile, sshfile and s3file with request.files: the most files one scrape reads, in name order; the rest are skipped and logged. Defaults to 100.

max_objects.description: kubernetes: the most objects a listing may hold; one more fails the scrape. Defaults to 10000.

max_open_connections.description: sshfile: the most SSH connections the collector holds open at once, across its hosts; its connections are then its own, shared with no other collector. A scrape that needs another at the limit closes the one used longest ago that no read holds, or waits within its deadline for one to be free. Defaults to 0, no limit. See docs/SSHFILE.md#persistent-connections.

max_response_bytes.description: http, graphite, grpc, localfile, sshfile and s3file: the most bytes of an answer, or of a file, the collector reads, decompressed. kubernetes: the most bytes of a page of the listing, and of the objects listed without their managed fields. sql: the most bytes of the values the statement's rows hold, text and binary data by their length and every other value as 8, each with its column's name's length, a NULL counting nothing. 10MiB when neither it nor limits.max_response_bytes is set. A size: a whole number of bytes, or a number with a unit such as 512KiB, 10MB or 1.5GiB, under 2^63 bytes. At least 1KiB, since a limit under it is one whose unit was left out; 0, like the key left out, is the default. The range, and the least of a size written as text, in quotes or with a unit, are checked by the exporter when the configuration loads.

max_rows.description: sql: the most rows the statement may return; one more fails the scrape. Defaults to 10000.

max_total_bytes.description: localfile, sshfile and s3file with request.files: the most one scrape reads across every file; a file that would go past it is refused. Defaults to 64 MiB.

message.description: grpc: the request message in the protobuf JSON mapping. Defaults to {}. May contain {{param_name}} placeholders, written as |json for a string, |number for a number, or |raw. The message probe parameter replaces it.

metadata.description: grpc: request metadata. Keys are lower-case; -bin keys and the ones gRPC reserves are refused. Values may contain {{param_name}} placeholders.

namespaces.description: kubernetes: the namespaces listed, each at its own path, in this order. Left out, with all_namespaces false, the exporter's own namespace, from its service account.

options.description: sql: the driver's settings, from a short list for each: postgres sslmode and application_name; mysql tls; sqlserver encrypt; oracle ssl; clickhouse protocol, compress and secure; snowflake warehouse, role and schema; vertica tlsmode. See docs/SQL.md#drivers.

pagination.description: http: fetch the further pages of a paginated answer and merge them into one JSON document, the first page with its items array holding every page's items, which the decoder and the rules read as the answer. Every page is sent the request's headers, credentials and body, and must stay on the target's scheme, host and port. The decoder is json. See docs/REQUESTS.md#pagination.

items.description: Required. The jq path of the array each page holds its items in, such as .items, .data.results, or . for a page that is an array. The merged answer is the first page with this array holding the items of every page, in order.

max_pages.description: The most pages one trip fetches, the first included: from 1 to 1000, 10 when left out. A trip that stops here with another page to come is answered with the pages it fetched, counted in http_exporter_pagination_max_pages_reached_total and logged.

next.description: Required with type next_url and cursor, and for no other: the jq expression of the next page's URL, absolute or relative to the page's, or of its cursor, read from the page, with $headers and $status as in a rule. null, false or "" ends the pages.

param.description: Required with type cursor, page and offset, and for no other: the query parameter the cursor, the page number or the offset is sent in. It replaces a parameter of that name in the target's query; request.query may not set it.

size.description: offset: how far the offset moves from one page to the next. Left out, by the number of items the page held.

start.description: page and offset: the first page's number, 1 when left out, or offset, 0 when left out. The first page is asked for with it.

type.description: Required. How the next page is found. link: the URL of the Link header's rel="next" (RFC 8288). next_url: the URL next reads from the page. cursor: the value next reads from the page, sent as the query parameter param. page: a page number in param, from start, one more each page. offset: an offset in param, from start, moved on by the items each page holds, or by size.

passphrase_file.description: sshfile, with private_key_file: the file of the passphrase an encrypted private key is decrypted with.

password_file.description: sshfile: the file of the account's password, tried after private_key_file; one of the two is required. sql: the file of the account's password, read when a connection is made.

path.description: http and graphite: joined onto the target URL; it cannot hold ? or #, and query parameters go under request.query. localfile: the file, relative to request.root and joined after the target. sshfile: the file on the host, relative to request.root. s3file: the object, relative to request.root, its key the two joined. May contain {{param_name}} or {{param_name:default}} path parameters, filled by param_<name> probe parameters.

path_style.description: s3file: name the bucket in the URL's path, endpoint/bucket/key, rather than its host, bucket.endpoint/key, as MinIO and most stores reached by address need. Defaults to false.

private_key_file.description: sshfile: the file of the private key the account authenticates with, tried before password_file. sql, the snowflake driver: the unencrypted PKCS#8 RSA key of key-pair authentication, instead of password_file. Read when a connection is made, so a key replaced on disk is used by the next one. See docs/SSHFILE.md#authentication and docs/SQL.md#authentication.

proto_files.description: grpc with descriptors: proto: the .proto files that define the service, compiled when the configuration loads and again when one changes.

proto_import_paths.description: grpc with descriptors: proto: the directories imports are resolved in, as protoc -I. Defaults to the directory of each file. The well-known types are built in.

protoset_file.description: grpc with descriptors: protoset: a FileDescriptorSet with its imports, as protoc --descriptor_set_out --include_imports or buf build -o writes it. Read again when it changes.

query.description: http and graphite: query parameters added to the request, after the target's own query, each name and value sent escaped. A name is not empty and holds no control character. Values may contain {{param_name}} placeholders.

record_type.description: dns: the record type asked for, in any case and with blanks around it or not: A, the default, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, SRV, or PTR, whose target is an IP address. See docs/DNS.md.

redirect_trusted_hosts.description: http and graphite: the hosts, besides the origin the request is made to, that a followed redirect may carry the collector's headers, credentials and request body to, and present its TLS client certificate to: host names, globs such as *.example.com, whose star matches dots too, and single IP addresses, each trusted on every port; "*" trusts every host. Matched against the host the redirect names as it is written there, which is never looked up: a final dot is part of the name, and an internationalised name is listed, and matched, in its xn-- form. No probe parameter sets it.

region.description: s3file: the region requests are signed for, as the store names it, such as eu-west-1, auto for R2. Defaults to the AWS SDK's (AWS_REGION, the shared config), else us-east-1. s3file is in a build with OPT_IN_REQUEST_TYPES naming it alone. See docs/S3FILE.md.

resource.description: kubernetes, required: the plural name of the resource listed, as kubectl api-resources lists it, such as pods, deployments or certificates. The core group's secrets are refused. See docs/KUBERNETES.md.

attempts.description: How many times a failed request is retried, from 0, the default, to 10.

backoff.description: A duration such as 500ms, 30s or 5m. Zero may be written 0, the one number that needs no unit.

codes.description: grpc: the gRPC status codes that are retried, by name, such as [UNAVAILABLE, ABORTED]. Defaults to [UNAVAILABLE]; OK is refused.

non_idempotent.description: http and graphite: retry a request whose method is not idempotent, such as POST, which sending again may repeat. Unset, only GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, PUT and DELETE requests are retried.

retry_after.description: http and graphite: wait what a retried answer's Retry-After header asks for, seconds or an HTTP date, instead of backoff. A value that is neither falls back to backoff; one longer than the probe's time left ends the request at once with that answer. Off by default: the header is not read.

statuses.description: http and graphite: the HTTP statuses that are retried, written as accept_status is, such as [404, 503] or ["5xx", 429]. Defaults to [408, 425, 429, "5xx"]; a list replaces the default, and [] retries no status, while a failed connection is retried still. An entry accept_status accepts whole is refused.

root.description: localfile, sshfile and s3file, required: the absolute directory the collector may read files under, on the exporter's filesystem or on the host, or, for s3file, the key prefix written as one, /exports/app for the keys under exports/app/. No read reaches outside it, through .. or a symbolic link. Not / for localfile; / is taken for sshfile, for an account confined to its own tree, and for s3file, for every key of the bucket. See docs/LOCALFILE.md, docs/SSHFILE.md and docs/S3FILE.md.

rpc.description: grpc, required: the method called, package.Service/Method, such as grpc.health.v1.Health/Check. See docs/GRPC.md.

secret_access_key_file.description: s3file, with access_key_id_file: the file of the static access key's secret.

server.description: dns: the server every question is sent to, host or host:port, port 53 when left out; the system's resolver, as /etc/resolv.conf names it, when the key is left out.

service_name.description: sql, required for the oracle driver and for no other: the service of the database.

session_token_file.description: s3file, with access_key_id_file and secret_access_key_file: the file of a temporary access key's session token.

statement.description: sql, required: the one statement run, written with the driver's own placeholders for args ($1 for postgres, ? for mysql, clickhouse, snowflake and vertica, @p1 for sqlserver, :1 for oracle). Its rows are read by a csv transform by column name, and by jq, yq and python as a list of objects. See docs/SQL.md#the-statement.

targets.description: graphite, required: the Graphite expressions asked of the render API, each sent as a target parameter, such as app.*.requests.count. May contain {{param_name}} placeholders, filled with letters, digits and _ - . : @ % + ~ only. See docs/GRAPHITE.md.

server_name.description: The name the target's certificate is checked against, and sent as SNI, when the target is addressed by something else, such as an IP address. Unset, the target's host.

transport.description: dns: udp, the default, which asks again over TCP for an answer too long for UDP, or tcp, which asks over TCP alone.

type.description: Required. How the collector reaches its data.

until.description: graphite: the end of the render window. Defaults to now. The until probe parameter overrides it.

username.description: sshfile and sql, required: the account the file is read as on the host, or the statement runs as on the database. Not blanks alone.

version.description: kubernetes: the resource's API version, such as v1 or v1beta1. Defaults to v1.

charset.description: The encoding of the response when the target does not declare it or declares it wrongly, and of local files: a WHATWG name such as windows-1252, iso-8859-2, windows-1251 or shift_jis. See docs/CONFIGURATION.md#character-encodings.

delimiter.description: csv decoder: the one character between fields, any but a double quote and a line break. Defaults to a comma. For a tab, write "\t" in double quotes, where YAML reads \t as the tab character.

invalid_lines.description: graphite decoder: what a carbon line that cannot be read does: fail the decode, the default, or skip, leaving it out, counted in http_exporter_decoder_lines_skipped_total and logged.

max_age.description: graphite decoder: leave out a series whose newest point is older than this, so a series nobody writes any more is not exported with its last value.

value.description: graphite decoder: how a series' points become its value: last, the newest point, by default, or max, min, avg or sum.

exclude.description: prometheus without metrics rules: drop the metrics whose name one of these regular expressions matches, anywhere in the name as the target gives it, also when include matches it. An entry is not empty and not blanks alone: '.*' matches every name.

include.description: prometheus without metrics rules: keep only the metrics whose name one of these regular expressions matches, anywhere in the name as the target gives it. Left out, every metric is kept. An entry is not empty and not blanks alone: '.*' matches every name.

labels.description: Constant labels given to every metric the collector exports, over a label of the same name a rule gave. A value written "" is the label left out. Values may contain {{param_name}} placeholders, filled from the probe's parameters. See docs/CONFIGURATION.md#collector-wide-labels.

items.description: A bundled Python library the script uses. Declared libraries are imported when the interpreter starts.

pre_script.description: Python run before the transform. It receives data and must leave its result in data.

items.description: A bundled Python library the script uses. Declared libraries are imported when the interpreter starts.

script.description: Python for the python transform. It emits metrics with metric(...).

type.description: How metrics are extracted from the decoded response. Required.

otlp.description: OTLP export of probe results, self-metrics and static targets with export_via_otlp. Off until enabled is true; a block that sets any other key must say enabled, true or false. See docs/OTLP.md.

batch_max_bytes.description: The most bytes the body of one export request may hold before compression, such as 4MiB; an export of more is sent as several requests, one after another, and a data point larger alone is sent in a request of its own. A size: a whole number of bytes, or a number with a unit such as 512KiB, 10MB or 1.5GiB. At least 64KiB, which the exporter checks of a size written as text, in quotes or with a unit, when the configuration loads; 0, like the key left out, is the default, 4MiB.

batch_max_size.description: The most data points one export request carries; an export of more is sent as several requests, one after another. Defaults to 8192.

compression.description: Compression of the export requests: gzip, the default, or none.

enabled.description: Turn the export on. false keeps the block's settings without using them.

endpoint.description: OTLP/HTTP metrics endpoint, such as http://otel-collector:4318/v1/metrics.

headers.description: Headers sent with every export request, such as a tenant or an API key. Once the block is switched on, a name is an HTTP token, set once whatever its case, and not Accept-Encoding.

interval.description: How often the points waiting are exported. At least 1s, which the exporter checks when the configuration loads; defaults to 30s.

max_pending_points.description: The most data points kept waiting for export while the endpoint fails; past it the oldest are dropped and counted. Defaults to 100000.

probe_attributes.description: Add collector and target attributes to the points a probe queues, so probes of different targets or collectors answering the same series are exported apart. Off, the default, the later probe's point replaces the earlier's.

timeout.description: How long one export attempt may take. Defaults to 5s. Also bounds the last export at shutdown.

unready_after_failures.description: Answer /ready with 503 after this many failed exports in a row, until one gets through. 0, the default, never does: an exporter whose exports fail still answers probes.

basic_auth.description: Basic authentication on the exporter's own endpoints. Off until enabled is true; a block that sets any other key must say enabled, true or false. Once enabled, username holds no colon, which ends the username in a Basic credential (RFC 7617).

enabled.description: Require the credentials. false keeps the block's settings without using them.

password_file.description: Read the password from this file instead of password, such as a mounted Secret. Read again when it changes.

username_file.description: Read the username from this file instead of username, such as a mounted Secret. Read again when it changes.
